summary: Defines managed objects that describe the behavior of an SNMPv2 entity itself, so a manager can inspect how the agent is running. It was replaced by RFC 3418.

eli5.summary: A device needs a page of facts about its own management software. This note lists those facts so a network manager can read them.

questions: how to query snmp agent information
subtitle: The standard set of managed objects that let a manager ask an SNMPv2 device about itself and its own SNMP traffic.

tldr.problem: A network manager needs a common way to ask any SNMPv2 device what it is, how long it has been running, and how its own SNMP software is behaving.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1907 defines the SNMPv2-MIB module: a system group (name, contact, location, uptime, services), a table of supported capabilities, an snmp group of counters, notification definitions such as coldStart, and a set-coordination lock.
tldr.outcome: It is a Draft Standard that obsoleted RFC 1450 and was itself obsoleted by RFC 3418.

today: RFC 1907 is a Draft Standard that was obsoleted by RFC 3418, so new work should use that document. It replaced RFC 1450.

sections.title: Purpose of the SNMPv2 MIB
sections.content:
A management system has agents on the nodes being managed, at least one management station, and a management protocol that carries information between them. The information is viewed as a collection of managed objects in a virtual store called the Management Information Base (MIB). MIB modules are written in a subset of ASN.1 called the Structure of Management Information (SMI).

RFC 1907 defines the managed objects that describe the behavior of an SNMPv2 entity itself. It also uses the term SNMPv1 for the original framework and SNMPv2 for the current one.
sections.eli5: A manager needs to ask a device questions about itself. This note writes down the list of questions every device should be able to answer.

sections.title: The System Group
sections.content:
The system group holds objects common to all managed systems, under mib-2 number 1. It includes sysDescr (a text description, up to 255 characters, with hardware, operating system and networking software), sysObjectID (the vendor's identifier for the management subsystem, allocated under the enterprises subtree 1.3.6.1.4.1) and sysUpTime (hundredths of a second since the management portion was last re-initialized).

Three objects are read-write: sysContact, sysName (by convention the fully-qualified domain name) and sysLocation. Unknown values are the zero-length string.

sysServices is a value from 0 to 127 that is a sum. For each layer L from 1 to 7 at which the node performs transactions, 2 raised to (L - 1) is added. A node that only routes has 4, and a host offering application services has 72.
sections.eli5: It is the name tag of the device: what it is, who to call about it, where it sits and how long it has been running.

sections.title: Capabilities Table and SNMP Counters
sections.content:
The sysORTable lists the capabilities of the local agent with respect to various MIB modules. Each row has an index (sysORIndex), an identifier (sysORID), a text description (sysORDescr) and the sysORUpTime at which the row was last instantiated. Entities that can change their MIB support have a varying number of rows, and sysORLastChange records when any row changed.

The snmp group (under mib-2 number 11) provides basic instrumentation and control. Its counters include snmpInPkts, snmpInBadVersions, snmpInBadCommunityNames, snmpInBadCommunityUses and snmpInASNParseErrs. snmpSilentDrops and snmpProxyDrops count requests dropped silently, for example because the reply would be too large or a proxy target failed.

snmpEnableAuthenTraps (enabled(1) or disabled(2)) overrides any configuration and can switch off all authenticationFailure traps. The RFC strongly recommends storing it in non-volatile memory.
sections.eli5: One list says which kinds of questions the device can answer. A set of tally counters records how many messages came in and how many were bad or dropped.

sections.title: Notifications and the Set Lock
sections.content:
Two objects, snmpTrapOID and snmpTrapEnterprise, describe the notification being sent. snmpTrapOID occurs as the second varbind in every SNMPv2-Trap-PDU and InformRequest-PDU.

The well-known traps are coldStart (the entity is reinitializing and its configuration may have changed), warmStart (reinitializing with configuration unaltered) and authenticationFailure (a message that is not properly authenticated was received). Link traps are defined in RFC 1573 and egpNeighborLoss in RFC 1213.

snmpSetSerialNo is an advisory lock that lets several cooperating managers coordinate their use of the set operation. The RFC calls it coarse-grain coordination.
sections.eli5: When something important happens, the device can ring a bell, such as I just restarted or someone with the wrong password knocked. A shared sign-up sheet stops two managers changing the same thing at once.

sections.title: Conformance and Obsolete Objects
sections.content:
The compliance statement snmpBasicCompliance makes four groups mandatory: the snmp group, the set group, the system group and the basic notifications group. The basic notifications group contains coldStart and authenticationFailure, the two notifications an entity is required to implement. The community group is mandatory only for entities that support community-based authentication.

The section also keeps a long list of SNMPv1-era counters (for example snmpOutPkts, snmpInGetRequests and snmpInTraps) with status obsolete. Their definitions from RFC 1213 were made obsolete by including a subset of the snmp group in this MIB.
sections.eli5: There is a short checklist of things every device must support. Some old counters are crossed off the list but kept so nobody reuses their numbers.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The security section of RFC 1907 is one sentence: security issues are not discussed in this memo. The MIB does include the authenticationFailure notification and the snmpEnableAuthenTraps switch, but the RFC gives no wider security analysis.
sections.eli5: This note does not talk about safety rules. It only provides the tally counters and the alarm switch.
